task: make a donation online (GoFundMe, charity websites, donation platforms): pick the campaign or organization, choose an amount and one-time vs monthly, enter payment details, handle the platform-tip step if shown, commit; complete when the thank-you / donation receipt is on screen. Surface pinned: a fundraising platform or charity website. Variants: starting your own fundraiser, Kickstarter-style reward pledges, and donating goods in person do not belong.

tree.label: Make an online donation
tree.note: 1 unless the video opens on the giving page. then 2 - every church keeper checks the street address before typing an amount, and 2.8 is what happens when the recipient is not on the platform. then 3, with 3.6 wherever the form asks it - lJrN asks it before the amount, K5dl and RkAM as a tab, aNEF and AWIG as a checkbox after the amount. 4 where the platform adds a tip, a fee cover or a match. 5 where the form asks who the gift is from. 6 where the platform puts it: nowhere for khD3, 4Cqd, Han7, lJrN and RLUw; a guest exit at the door for ZcNV; after the amounts for K5dl, n-lH, RkAM and GYik; before anything in the apps - aNEF, qWf2, AWIG, qQi3. 7 then 8, except that aNEF and SaD3 run 7.3 before 3 because the app wants a stored method first. 9 after the commit; RLUw gets 9.2 before any money moves because the platform emails the bank details.

children.label: Reach the giving platform
children.note: 1.1, 1.2 or 1.4 gets to the form; 1.3 before the form on the one platform that teaches it. 1.5 for each prompt the app raises. 1.6 for the one keeper who starts from a text message. 1.7 first on a shared machine.

questions.question: Is the organization named on this page the one you asked to give to?
questions.why: The screen showed a banner asking for a $2.75 donation to keep Wikipedia thriving, prompting the choice of who to support.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means losing the personal satisfaction of selecting a cause that aligns with your own values.
questions.check: Which organization does the page name as the recipient of the gift?
questions.say_example: This page is asking for money for <Wikipedia>. You asked to give to <the Red Cross>. I'll go to their page instead.

questions.question: What address should you type to reach the giving site?
questions.why: The screen shows an empty browser tab with the address bar focused, requiring you to know the exact web address of the giving platform to proceed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to ensure the agent navigates to the correct, trusted giving platform for their specific church.
questions.check: What address is shown in the address bar?
questions.say_example: Opened <redcross.org>.

questions.question: Does the address in the bar belong to the organization the page claims to be?
questions.why: Checking the address bar to confirm the exact URL ensures you are on the legitimate charity website before proceeding.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally verify the website's authenticity, which is a critical step to avoid fraudulent charity scams.
questions.check: What domain is in the address bar, and what organization name does the page header show?
questions.say_example: The address is <redcross-gifts.net>. The charity's own site is <redcross.org>. This isn't it, so I'll stop here.

questions.question: Is this page secure enough to type your card number into?
questions.why: Checking the padlock icon and the 'Connection is secure' popup ensures your credit card numbers are encrypted before you submit them.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally verify the site's security certificate and ensure your financial data is being transmitted safely.
questions.check: Does the address bar show 'Not secure' or a warning instead of the padlock?
questions.say_example: This page says not secure. Your card number wouldn't be protected here, so I won't enter it. I'll look for the charity's own donate page.

questions.question: Which app from the search results should you install?
questions.why: The screen shows multiple donation apps like 'Givelify' and 'GiveTide', so you must identify the correct one to ensure the donation goes through the intended platform.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to verify that the agent selected the specific, trusted platform they intended to use rather than a similarly named alternative.
questions.check: Who is listed as the developer of each app in the results?
questions.say_example: There are <three> giving apps here. <Pushpay> is the one <your church> named, so I'll install that one. OK, or pick another?

questions.question: Is this the official app for the organization?
questions.why: The screen shows the 'Adventist Giving' app in the App Store, and you must verify it is the official platform before proceeding.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to personally verify the app's authenticity and reviews before trusting it with your financial information.
questions.check: Who is listed as the developer of this app, and does the listing name the organization or its giving platform?
questions.say_example: This app is made by <Acme Apps>. <The church> didn't make it, and neither did <Pushpay>. It might be a lookalike, so I won't use it.

questions.question: Should the app get your location to find nearby charities?
questions.why: The app prompts you to enable your location so it can instantly locate charities or places of worship near you.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: If the agent makes this choice, you lose control over your privacy and whether the app is allowed to track your physical location.
questions.check: Does a prompt ask to allow location access?
questions.say_example: Said no to location.

questions.question: Do you want to allow the app to send you notifications?
questions.why: The app prompts for permission to send alerts, sounds, and icon badges, which determines whether you will receive future interruptions from the platform.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses control over their personal device preferences and might receive unwanted alerts if the agent automatically accepts.
questions.check: Does a prompt ask to allow notifications?
questions.say_example: Said no to notifications.

questions.question: Do you want to turn on Face ID for this app?
questions.why: The app asks if you want to keep your personal information secure by requiring Face ID to access it.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent cannot provide your biometric data or decide your preferred level of device-linked security for this app.
questions.check: Does a prompt ask to enable Face ID?
questions.say_example: Skipped Face ID setup.

questions.question: Do you want to send the gift by text yourself, with this code and amount?
questions.why: The messaging screen requires entering the organization's specific text-to-give number and your desired donation amount to initiate the transaction.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means the agent decides the donation amount and recipient number, potentially pledging more money than you intended.
questions.check: What number and keyword does the page say to text, and how does it say to write the amount?
questions.say_example: This site takes gifts by text. Send <GIVE 50> to <73256> from your phone. That text is the gift itself. Want to do that, or give on the website instead?

questions.question: Is the site signed in as someone other than you?
questions.why: The navigation bar shows an active session under 'Me', which means the donation could incorrectly default to the logged-in user's information.

questions.check: What account name does the navigation bar show as signed in?
questions.say_example: This site is signed in as <Maria>. The gift would go under her name and card. I'll sign out first.

questions.question: Are you fully logged out of the account?
questions.why: Seeing the 'Login' and 'Register' links in the navigation menu confirms that your session has been securely closed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you cannot personally verify that your account session was securely terminated after the transaction.
questions.check: Does the navigation show Login and Register links instead of an account name?
questions.say_example: Signed out of <Maria's> account before starting.

questions.question: What should you search for to find the campaign?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the peace of mind of personally verifying that your specific local church is officially registered to receive funds on this platform.

questions.say_example: <Grace Church> shows as not enrolled here. A gift can't go through on this site. I'll look for their own giving page.

questions.question: Is the campaign's goal the same on the listing and on its page?
questions.why: The search result and edit page show a £100 target while the campaign page displays £200, which might indicate a platform glitch or a deceptive listing.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to spot this discrepancy and potentially avoid donating to a suspicious or buggy campaign.

questions.say_example: The listing says the goal is <100 pounds>. The campaign page says <200>. The two don't agree, so I'm not sure this listing is right.

questions.question: Did the button open a donation form, or an event sign-up?
questions.why: The page presents distinct options to either 'DONATE' or 'RIDE WITH ME', requiring you to choose the correct path for a financial gift.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to ensure the agent selects the direct donation path rather than accidentally registering them as an event participant.
questions.check: Does the page that opened ask for a gift amount, or for participant registration or new-fundraiser details?
questions.say_example: This button signs you up as a participant. It doesn't give money. Going back to the donate button.

questions.question: Is this giving page for the organization you named, at the location you named?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the peace of mind of personally verifying that the donation portal belongs to your specific local community.

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the critical human judgment needed to distinguish a legitimate, family-authorized campaign from a well-disguised scam.
